source.title: CDFP-Net: Cross-Modal Dynamic Fusion with Diffusion Priors for PET-CT Tumor Segmentation
source.checked_scope: Methods and directional ablation table, selected paper-body reading
source.source_claim_paraphrase: The authors compare PET-query-CT against the reversed query direction under matching parameter count, and report an aggregate DSC advantage for the former.

analysis.research_object: Patient-level expected utility of modality query direction at fixed compute budget
analysis.hidden_assumption: An average direction benefit applies equally across individual lesions
alternatives: Direction benefit is approximately constant across relevant cases
Direction benefit varies and is prospectively predictable using case features
analysis.proposed_test: Paired per-case direction analysis with held-out condition-based routing; matched compute and model capacity
analysis.boundary: Average ablation does not prove prospectively predictable case-level routing; the paper already contains reverse-direction ablation

presentation.reader_goal: Differentiate architectural priors, marginal gains, and identifiable patient-conditional benefits
